discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of time-reversal-invariant topological insulators (the quantum spin Hall effect)
subfield: Condensed matter physics: topological phases of matter
motivation: In 2005 Kane and Mele showed that spin-orbit coupling in a simple honeycomb model produces a new phase of matter: a time-reversal-invariant insulator with protected helical edge states. They identified the Z2 topological invariant that separates it from an ordinary insulator. This was a new kind of topological order that needs no magnetic field, and it answered a question the quantum Hall effect had left open. In 2007 Molenkamp's group measured quantized edge conductance in HgTe quantum wells and confirmed the quantum spin Hall state. The Z2 classification soon extended to three dimensions, and ARPES then found topological surface states in bismuth compounds. The work started a large field. Topological insulators, topological superconductors and the wider classification of symmetry-protected phases all build on it. It is a clear example of a deep, simple theoretical model that revealed a phenomenon no one expected, followed by a decisive experiment that confirmed it.
